newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Van Leer sees 9 pct earnings growth in 97.
newsitem.headline: Van Leer sees 9 pct earnings growth in 97.

text.p: Dutch industrial and consumer packaging group Van Leer NV said on Monday it expected to post earnings growth of some 9-10 percent in 1997.

Van Leer chairman Bill de Vlugt told a results news conference that earnings per share over 1996 had been cosmetically boosted by the fact they were calculated according to the weighted average of shares outstanding in 1996 rather than the number outstanding at year-end.
"But that is of course a one-off bonus, which means we will have to boost net profits by at least nine percent to simply retain the same earnings per share," De Vlugt said.
"Van Leer is well-positioned to further increase profitability," he added.

Asked whether this meant the company was expecting double-digit earnings growth, he countered: "Isn't nine percent enough?" before adding Van Leer could be expected to post an improvement in earnings of around 10 percent.

Van Leer earlier reported earnings per share rose 39.4 percent to 3.22 guilders in 1996, outstripping a record 22.4 percent growth to 96.9 million guilders in net profits available to ordinary shareholders.
This was because the weighted average of shares outstanding through 1996 amounted to 30.14 million, while the number outstanding at year-end amounted to 34.25 million.
This reflected the combined effect of a conversion into preference shares in December and the issue of new shares when Van Leer launched on the Amsterdam Stock Exchange in May 1996.
